content: Health behaviors, such as condom use and contraceptive use, play a critical role in sexual and reproductive health outcomes, including the prevention of sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and unintended pregnancies. PICO Question 2: What interventions can support women living with HIV (WLHIV) in safely disclosing their HIV status, particularly when they fear violence or are currently experiencing violence? Population (P): Women living with HIV who fear violence or disclose that they are currently experiencing violence. Intervention (I): Comparison (C): No intervention. Outcomes: 1. 2. Incidence of violence (physical, sexual, or emotional). 3. Fear of violence. 4. Other adverse events, such as relationship dissolution, abandonment, job loss, loss of children, or loss of access to services. 5. Positive outcomes, including feelings of empowerment, safety, partner involvement, improved physical health, engagement in HIV care and treatment, and adherence to antiretroviral therapy (ART). PICO Question 3: What delivery methods result in the best maternal and perinatal outcomes for women living with HIV? Population (P): Women living with HIV and their children. Intervention (I): Elective cesarean section (C-section). Comparison (C): Other delivery methods, such as non-elective C-section or vaginal delivery. Outcomes: 1. HIV infection rates in children born to WLHIV, focusing on the efficacy of preventing vertical transmission. 2. Maternal morbidity and mortality, including febrile morbidity, endometritis, hemorrhage, severe anemia, pneumonia, and urinary tract infections. 3. Infant morbidity and mortality, including respiratory conditions (e.g., respiratory distress syndrome, transient tachypnea of the newborn) and skin lacerations. 4. Breastfeeding outcomes, including the success and timing of initiation and continuation. PICO Question 4: Do the outcomes of medical and surgical abortion differ between women living with HIV and HIV-uninfected women? Population (P): Women seeking an abortion. Intervention (I): Medical abortion among WLHIV. Comparison (C): Medical abortion among HIV-uninfected women. Outcomes: 1. 2. Serious adverse events, such as death, hospitalization, or the need for blood transfusion. 3. Other adverse outcomes and side effects, including hemorrhage not requiring transfusion and vomiting. 4. Patient satisfaction. Key Literature and Systematic Reviews: 1. Beres et al. (2017) conducted a systematic review on non-specialist psychosocial support interventions for WLHIV, highlighting their impact on health outcomes. 2. Narasimhan et al. (2016) explored aging and healthy sexuality among WLHIV, emphasizing the intersection of sexual health and aging. 3. Chop et al. (2017) reviewed the relationship between food insecurity, sexual risk behaviors, and ART adherence among WLHIV. 4. Kennedy et al.
